title: Trevino Takes the Stage Alone as Cigarroa Skips Mayoral Runoff Forum
excerpt: Mayor Victor Trevino answered questions alone at a City Hall mayoral runoff forum Wednesday night after Councilmember Alyssa Cigarroa withdrew a day earlier, citing concerns about fairness — leaving voters to hear from only one of the two runoff candidates.
content:
Mayor Dr. Victor D. Trevino took the stage alone Wednesday night at a mayoral runoff forum at City Hall, after his opponent, District 8 Councilmember Alyssa Cigarroa, withdrew from the event a day earlier.

The forum was part of the city’s Laredo Votes 2026 voter education campaign, meant to give residents a chance to hear directly from both candidates ahead of the December 12 runoff. Cigarroa notified the city on Tuesday, November 17, that she would not take part, citing concerns about fairness and impartiality and what she described as preferential treatment of Trevino by the city, including on its social media.

The city said its participation requirements were shared during mandatory orientations and applied consistently to candidates in the forum series.

It was not the first city-hosted mayoral forum Cigarroa missed. She also did not take part in the city’s October 8 forum, when the Public Information Office cited a prior engagement. She has taken part in other forums during the campaign, including events hosted by the Kiwanis Club of Laredo and Texas A&M International University, where she spoke about water infrastructure, government accountability, long-term planning, economic development and city finances.

Cigarroa and Trevino advanced out of a five-candidate field in the November 3 election. Cigarroa finished first with 35.54 percent of the vote, followed by Trevino with 32.29 percent — a gap of 1,785 votes, according to unofficial results.

With Cigarroa absent, Trevino faced six questions from Univision and Fox Laredo reporter Miriam Salinas. On downtown development, he said the city needs to offer incentives to businesses and property owners while reviewing existing tax programs to see whether they are helping the area. On water, he pointed to the ongoing replacement of aging lines — about 40,000 linear feet of pipe replaced and roughly $130 million spent — and said the city is working to divide its water system into quadrants so future problems affect smaller areas instead of risking citywide boil-water notices.

Asked what the city could do when Bethany House reaches capacity, Trevino said homelessness has multiple causes and should not be approached with a single solution, and that officials need to identify whether people face psychological, physical or economic challenges and address those circumstances individually. On transparency, he pointed to an app the city is developing that would let residents track water problems, including where a break happened and how long repairs are expected to take. He also defended expanding the World Trade Bridge and other border infrastructure, citing the volume of commercial traffic moving through Laredo.

In his closing statement, Trevino said a mayor must bring education, experience, honesty and diplomacy to the job. “A mayor has to be present where there’s challenges, where there’s difficult situations,” he said.

After the forum, Trevino said he was disappointed Cigarroa did not attend and that voters should have the chance to hear from both candidates. “This should have been a debate, and my opponent did not show up,” he said. “When you’re a leader, you have to be there to answer questions.”

Cigarroa has said her decision does not mean she is stepping away from voters and that she will keep communicating with residents through other avenues. She is scheduled to take part in another mayoral forum hosted by the Laredo Chamber of Commerce on December 8, which will air on KGNS, giving voters another chance to hear both candidates directly before the December 12 runoff.

Update — November 25, 2026: The Laredo Chamber of Commerce moved its mayoral runoff forum to Wednesday, December 2, at 6:30 p.m., airing live on KGNS-TV 8 and KGNS+. It had originally been scheduled for December 8, the last day of early voting. Both candidates are expected to take part.

Sources: Laredo Chamber of Commerce, Nov. 19, 2026.
